hl.bind(modKey .. " + CTRL + B", hl.dsp.exec_cmd("blueman-manager"))              -- bluetooth
hl.bind(modKey .. " + CTRL + SHIFT + W", hl.dsp.exec_cmd("nm-connection-editor"))         -- wifi (moved off SUPER+CTRL+W for herdr search)
hl.bind(modKey .. " + CTRL + SHIFT + N", hl.dsp.exec_cmd("hyprsunset -t 4000"))           -- nightlight (moved off SUPER+CTRL+N for herdr new_workspace)
hl.bind(modKey .. " + CTRL + I", hl.dsp.exec_cmd("pkill hypridle || hypridle"))   -- toggle idle
hl.bind(modKey .. " + CTRL + E", hl.dsp.exec_cmd("rofi -modi emoji -show emoji")) -- emoji (needs rofi-emoji)
-- Wallpaper -> transition map (keyed by filename). Files not listed here use
-- `default_transition`. Valid names (see `yinctl --list-trans`):
--   bookflip  bounce  box  chessboard  mosaic  static  zoom
local wallpaper_transitions = {
  ["gojo-eye.mp4"]              = "zoom",
  ["gojo.mp4"]                  = "bookflip",
  ["latios-latias.jpg"]         = "static",
  -- sddm-bg-frame.png, sleeping-snorlax.png -> default (static)
}
local default_transition = "static"

-- Render the map into POSIX-sh `case` arms so the picker stays async.
local case_arms = ""
for name, trans in pairs(wallpaper_transitions) do
  case_arms = case_arms .. string.format('    "%s") t="%s" ;;\n', name, trans)
end

hl.bind(modKey .. " + SHIFT + Space", hl.dsp.exec_cmd(string.format([[
pick="$(find ~/.config/hypr/wallpapers -type f | rofi -dmenu -i -p 'Wallpaper' -theme ~/.config/rofi/launchers/type-1/style-6.rasi)"
[ -z "$pick" ] && exit 0
case "$(basename "$pick")" in
%s    *) t="%s" ;;
esac
~/.config/hypr/scripts/set-wallpaper.sh "$pick" "$t"
]], case_arms, default_transition)))
hl.bind("CTRL + ALT + Delete", hl.dsp.exec_cmd("wlogout"))
 
-- ============================================================
--  SPEECH TO TEXT
-- ============================================================
hl.bind(modKey .. " + ALT + D", hl.dsp.exec_cmd("/home/krubics/.local/share/hyprwhspr/src/config/hyprland/hyprwhspr-tray.sh record"))

-- ============================================================
--  CAPTURE
-- ============================================================
hl.bind(modKey .. " + CTRL + S",   hl.dsp.exec_cmd("hyprshot -m region"))

--  MEDIA KEYS  (standard: wpctl / brightnessctl / playerctl)
-- ============================================================
hl.bind("XF86AudioRaiseVolume", hl.dsp.exec_cmd("wpctl set-volume -l 1.0 @DEFAULT_AUDIO_SINK@ 5%+"), { locked = true, repeating = true })
hl.bind("XF86AudioLowerVolume", hl.dsp.exec_cmd("wpctl set-volume @DEFAULT_AUDIO_SINK@ 5%-"),        { locked = true, repeating = true })
hl.bind("XF86AudioMute",        hl.dsp.exec_cmd("wpctl set-mute @DEFAULT_AUDIO_SINK@ toggle"),       { locked = true })
hl.bind("XF86AudioMicMute",     hl.dsp.exec_cmd("wpctl set-mute @DEFAULT_AUDIO_SOURCE@ toggle"),     { locked = true })
hl.bind("XF86MonBrightnessUp",   hl.dsp.exec_cmd("brightnessctl -e4 -n2 set 5%+"), { locked = true, repeating = true })

I'm seeing the same pattern emerge: pyprland's process tracking thinks the kitty window failed to spawn because it didn't appear within the timeout window, but the window actually did open eventually—just slower than pyprland's internal wait threshold, which aligns with that ~14.86 second delay I'm observing.

This is fundamentally a timing issue rather than a broken window-matching mechanism. Unlike the VSCode single-instance-lock problem where the process genuinely exits, here pyprland simply gave up waiting before the window materialized. I should look for a configurable spawn timeout I can increase, or investigate why kitty is taking 14+ seconds to start—whether that's `--class` overhead, general system load from all my testing, or something else entirely.

Since kitty's class is completely unique (`kitty-scratch-term`), applying the same fix that worked for VSCode—setting `process_tracking = false` and `match_by = "class"`—should be safe here. This bypasses the whole "wait for process to signal readiness" mechanism and just tracks by the window class, which the window rule already handles reliably regardless of spawn timing. plugins = [
    "scratchpads",
]

# Only the scratchpads plugin is enabled — no other pyprland feature
# (expose, magnify, monitors, wallpapers, etc.) is loaded or active.

# that must be told apart from ordinary terminal windows. Your SUPER+RETURN
# ghostty terminal is completely unaffected.

async def __wait_for_client(self, scratch: Scratch, use_proc: bool = True) -> bool:
        """Wait for a client to be up and running.

        if `match_by=` is used, will use the match criteria, else the process's PID will be used.

        Args:
            scratch: The scratchpad object
            use_proc: whether to use the process object
        """
        self.log.info("==> Wait for %s spawning", scratch.uid)
        interval_range = [0.1] * 10 + [0.2] * 20 + [0.5] * 15
        for interval in interval_range:
            await asyncio.sleep(interval)
            is_alive = await scratch.is_alive()

            # skips the checks if the process isn't started (just wait)
            if is_alive or not use_proc:
                info = await scratch.fetch_matching_client()
                if info:
                    await scratch.update_client_info(info)
                    self.log.info(
                        "=> %s client (proc:%s, addr:%s) detected on time",
                        scratch.uid,
                        scratch.pid,
                        scratch.full_address,
                    )
                    self.scratches.register(scratch)
                    self.scratches.clear_state(scratch, "respawned")
                    return True
            if use_proc and not is_alive:
                return False
        return False

    async def _start_scratch_nopid(self, scratch: Scratch) -> bool:
        """Ensure alive, PWA version.

        Args:
            scratch: The scratchpad object
        """
        uid = scratch.uid
        started = scratch.meta.no_pid
        if not await scratch.is_alive():
            started = False
        if not started:
            self.scratches.reset(scratch)
            await self.start_scratch_command(uid)
            r = await self.__wait_for_client(scratch, use_proc=False)
            scratch.meta.no_pid = r
            return r
        return True

    async def _start_scratch(self, scratch: Scratch) -> bool:
        """Ensure alive, standard version.

        Args:
            scratch: The scratchpad object
        """
        uid = scratch.uid
        if uid in self.procs:
            with contextlib.suppress(ProcessLookupError):
                self.procs[uid].kill()
            del self.procs[uid]  # ensure the old process is removed from the dict
        self.scratches.reset(scratch)
        await self.start_scratch_command(uid)
        self.log.info("starting %s", uid)
        if not await self.__wait_for_client(scratch):
            self.log.error("⚠ Failed spawning %s as proc %s", uid, scratch.pid)
            if await scratch.is_alive():
                error = "The command didn't open a window"
            else:
                await self.procs[uid].communicate()
                code = self.procs[uid].returncode
                error = f"The command failed with code {code}" if code else "The command terminated successfully, is it already running?"
            self.log.error('"%s": %s', scratch.conf["command"], error)
            await self.backend.notify_error(error)
            return False
        return True

    async def ensure_alive(self, uid: str) -> bool:
        """Ensure the scratchpad is started.

        Returns true if started

        Args:
            uid: The scratchpad name

        item = self.scratches.get(name=uid)

# Scratchpad Zen browser — isolated profile, forced new instance, and a

mkdir -p "$HOME/.zen-scratch"
exec zen --new-instance --profile "$HOME/.zen-scratch" \
  --new-window "file:///home/krubics/.config/hypr/scripts/zen-scratch-marker.html"

# Wayland app_id. kitty supports a real --class override (the pattern the
# official pyprland docs use), so it's the reliable choice for a scratchpad
# that must be told apart from ordinary terminal windows. Your SUPER+RETURN
# ghostty terminal is completely unaffected.
# match_by="class"/process_tracking=false here too: pyprland's default
# spawn-wait timeout is shorter than this system's kitty startup latency,
# so it gives up waiting even though the window reliably appears a moment
# later. `kitty-scratch-term` is a unique class (nothing else uses it), so
# class-based matching carries zero ambiguity risk.
[scratchpads.term]
command = "kitty --class kitty-scratch-term"
class = "kitty-scratch-term"
match_by = "class"
process_tracking = false
animation = "fromTop"
size = "75% 60%"
margin = 50
lazy = true

# Zen shares class="zen" across every window regardless of profile, so
# class-based matching can't distinguish this scratchpad instance from your
# regular Zen windows (verified: match_by="class" does a blind scan of all
# current windows, not a spawn-correlated one — unsafe here). The wrapper
# forces a fixed marker page title instead, which title-matching can key on
# without ambiguity. process_tracking stays off because Zen's cold start
# (fresh isolated profile) can exceed pyprland's internal spawn-wait window;
# title matching keeps working via event-driven re-matching regardless.
[scratchpads.browser]
command = "/home/krubics/.config/hypr/scripts/zen-scratch.sh"
class = "zen"
match_by = "title"
title = "re:.*zen-scratch-marker.*"
process_tracking = false
size = "85% 85%"
lazy = true
